minutes.headline: Committee voted for no change to bus policy, with no fee or expansion, and sent the facility-use policy back to subcommittee.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the FY23 five-year identified-needs staffing plan and the budget calendar. It reviewed school bus transportation options ahead of the January bid and chose to keep current policy. It also sent the facility-use policy back to subcommittee after the Parks Commission objected to the priority order. A new member was welcomed and a student asked for an athletic trainer.

public_comment.topic: Asked the committee to hire an athletic trainer for athlete safety, citing a survey and injuries; says the position is in the five-year plan but not budgeted.
Asked about the status of the field-use understanding with the Parks department and urged that no charges be imposed for use of school facilities.
Asked that the FY23 budget action show the impact of new positions on the 2.5 cap, whether the bus contract excuses payment when the state closes schools, and about a new facilities director.

decisions.decision: Facility-use policy 1202 goes back to the policy subcommittee for a further revision, including an indemnification check, annual and special town meeting wording, and meeting with the Parks Commission.
The chair will draft a Ledger article and social media posts on the committee's role, and the roles survey will be repeated around April or May.
Committee members favored keeping budget Q&A sessions on the agenda in February and March.
Revolving account reporting by the business manager to be annual rather than quarterly.
Turkey Hill discussion and a reorganization of subcommittees to be put on future agendas.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to make no change to school bus transportation policy, with no fee and no expansion, ahead of the January bus bid.
Policy 1202 on use of school facilities went back to the policy subcommittee for revision, including a meeting with the Parks Commission.
The committee voted to leave the town bylaws on schools as they are for this review and pass that to the bylaw committee.
Staff presented the FY23 identified needs and five-year staffing plan, noting that grant-funded positions, many through ESSER, expire in later years.
A resident asked the committee to hire an athletic trainer, saying the position is in the five-year plan but not budgeted.

why_it_matters: Keeping bus policy unchanged means no new fee and no added routes for families, while the new contract's projected increase is the cost the budget carries.
Positions paid by a grant that expires will need a new funding source or a decision to end them, and that choice will land in a future school budget and, mostly, in the town's taxes.
Rules on field and facility use affect local youth groups and the Parks Commission, and the revised policy will come back to the committee for another reading.
watch_next: The January bus bid, which sets the cost under the no-change policy.
The revised facility-use policy 1202 returning from the policy subcommittee.
